title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's mathematics. It is page 161 of a typed manuscript, photographed upside down, apparently a sheet whose blank back Grothendieck reused for his handwritten notes. The neighbouring pages are his notes on motivic Galois gerbes, Frobenius and Tate-module fibre functors, and H^2(Q,H). Its content matches Joseph Lipman's 'Rational singularities, with applications to algebraic surfaces and unique factorization' (Publ. Math. IHES 36, 1969), §25, Theorem 25.1 and Remark 25.2. This attribution is inferred from the content, the numbering ('CASE Vd of §24', 'Theorem 25.1') and the typescript style; it is not printed on the page. Presumably it is a preprint page.

The theorem characterises the E8 singularity as the unique non-regular two-dimensional factorial rational singularity with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic not 2, 3 or 5. Its completion is k[[u,v,w]]/(u^2+v^3+w^5).

The page finishes the proof:
- (i)⇒(ii): coordinate changes y' = y + (q/3α)x^2 - (u/3α)x^3 and x' = x + vy kill the lower-order coefficients p, q, r, s, t in the equation (6). This leaves a normal form of the type z^2 + αy^3 + βx^5 = 0 with α, β units.
- (ii)⇒(iii): in the henselization R*, the residue field is algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ 3, 5, so Hensel's lemma makes α a cube and β a fifth power. Rescaling gives the exact E8 equation.
- (iii)⇒(iv)⇒(i): by the Cohen structure theorem, R̂ is a quotient of R̄ = S/(u^2+v^3+w^5). R̄ is factorial (shown in §24, case Vd), hence a domain of dimension 2. So the surjection R̄ → R̂ between two-dimensional rings must be an isomorphism.
- Remark 25.2: in characteristic 2, 3 or 5 there are several possible normal forms (in Lipman's paper, several equations). The units α, β can be taken to be 1 when R is henselian.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. One justification is compressed: the step 'R̄ factorial, so R̂ = R̄' uses only that R̄ is a two-dimensional domain, so any proper quotient has smaller dimension; factoriality is more than is needed here.
Archival note: the page is misattributed if read as Grothendieck's work. It is a typescript page of Lipman's 1969 IHES paper, reused as scrap paper.

ideas.what: Characterisation of E8 (u^2+v^3+w^5) as the unique non-regular two-dimensional factorial complete local ring with a rational singularity, algebraically closed residue field, characteristic ≠ 2, 3, 5.
ideas.modern_name: Factoriality of the E8 rational double point; Lipman's theorem on two-dimensional UFDs
ideas.usually_credited_to: J. Lipman (1969). Complex-analytic case: Mumford (1961, topology) and Brieskorn (1967-68).

ideas.what: Coordinate changes and Hensel's lemma to normalise the equation to z^2+y^3+x^5.
ideas.modern_name: Normal forms of rational double points
ideas.where_published: Lipman 1969; M. Artin, 'Coverings of the rational double points in characteristic p' (1977)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of Lipman's published 1969 paper on rational singularities, found in the archive because Grothendieck wrote his motivic-Galois notes on the backs of preprint pages. It contains no unpublished Grothendieck mathematics. The only point of interest is archival: it hints at what preprints he had around the time of these notes (1969 or later, consistent with the archive's 'vers 1977' dating).
transcription_corrections: The page image is rotated 180°; the transcription is of the upside-down typed text.
'q = ux' should be checked against the image; it may be 'q = ux^2' or similar in the original. The image is ambiguous and only plausibly shows 'q = ux'.
This page is typed English text from Lipman's paper, not Grothendieck's handwriting; it does not continue the gerbe and H^2 discussion of the neighbouring pages.
